qs.q: In the MDA model, what are mechanics?
opts: The rules and actions in the code
qs.why: Mechanics are the rules. Dynamics grow out of them, and aesthetics are the feelings.

qs.q: What is a game's core loop?
opts: The set of actions players repeat over and over
qs.why: If the core loop is fun, the game is fun.

qs.q: Which genre is about running and jumping between platforms, seen from the side?
qs.why: Mario and Celeste are classic platformers.

qs.q: Mixing pixel art, photos and smooth cartoon art in one game makes it look richer.
qs.why: Pick one style and a small palette so everything belongs together.

opts: Small effects like particles, shake and sounds that make actions feel strong
qs.why: Juice is extra feedback, not extra rules.

qs.q: What does it mean to telegraph an attack?
opts: Show a clear warning before it hits
qs.why: Players accept getting hit when they could have seen it coming.

qs.q: In "teach, test, twist" level design, where should a new idea be introduced?
opts: Somewhere safe, where failing costs almost nothing
qs.why: Let players try the idea with nothing to lose first.

qs.q: Most testers quit at the same point in level 3. What is that called?
qs.why: Smooth it into smaller steps so the curve rises gently.

qs.q: Which is a gentle way to guide players toward a hidden area?
opts: A trail of coins leading to it
qs.why: Breadcrumbs pull players along and let them feel clever.

opts: The area where a character can be hit
The area of an attack that does damage
A box that stops you walking through walls
When the attacker's active hitbox overlaps the defender's hurtbox
Whenever the attack button is pressed
When the two characters are on screen
qs.why: It needs an active hitbox touching a hurtbox.
A ends exactly where B starts. Touching edges don't count as overlapping, so it's false.

qs.q: Fill in the missing operator so gravity changes the speed, not the position directly.
qs.why: Gravity adds to the falling speed each frame, and the speed moves the player.

qs.q: On a canvas, which way does y go?
qs.why: (0, 0) is the top-left corner, and y grows downward.

qs.q: Why give the player invincibility frames after a hit?
opts: So one touch doesn't take a life every single frame
qs.why: Without them, touching an enemy for 1 second would cost 60 lives.

opts: A few frames where you can still jump after walking off a ledge
Time spent on the title screen
The time before an enemy attacks
qs.why: It forgives players who press jump a moment too late.

qs.q: Tiles are 20 pixels. What does this print?
qs.why: 45 / 20 is 2.25, and Math.floor rounds it down to tile 2.
